shortDescription: Polish retail sales came in lower than analysts expected in August, and the pace of growth slowed compared to the previous month as slower wage growth and rising fuel prices began to impact the spending of some consumers.

children: Polish retail sales came in lower than analysts expected in August, and the pace of growth slowed compared to the previous month as slower wage growth and rising fuel prices began to impact the spending of some consumers.

Retail sales at constant prices (PLRSCO=ECI) grew 3.8% in August from a year earlier, according to data published on Tuesday by the statistical office. That compares with 3.9% in July and analysts' expectations of a 4.2% increase.
ING economists estimate the pace of private consumption growth to rise back above 3% year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026, following a 2.8% year-on-year increase in the second quarter.

"... the consumer is no longer as strong as in 2025. Investment will remain a key driver of economic growth. We currently estimate GDP growth in the third quarter of 2026 at around 3.5%," they wrote in a note.
Moderate consumer demand helps limit inflation, giving the Polish central bank the leeway to wait rather than make hasty decisions regarding interest rates, analysts said.
